runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed the week on a constructive note Saturday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 gaining 191 points (+0.29%) to 66,323, recovering from Thursday's modest decline as yen weakness offered exporters a tailwind and domestic data showed continued services sector resilience. The positive close came despite lingering unease from Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole address, which rippled through overnight currency markets, pushing the dollar index up 0.50% to 99.65. European bourses (DAX ~20,748, FTSE ~9,052) edged marginally higher in thin Friday trade, with energy names providing support while rate-sensitive real estate and utilities lagged on Bund yield widening.

On Wall Street Friday, the S&P 500 shed 0.25% to 7,711.76 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.52% to 26,402.42 — erasing most of the week's gains sparked by Nvidia's blockbuster earnings outlook — after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech stressed that 12-month PCE inflation 'stands at 3.7%' with 54% of the basket still rising faster than 3%. Futures markets closed pricing a 57% probability of a September rate hike, up sharply from ~35% before the speech. The two-year Treasury yield touched its highest level since July near 4.32% and gold cratered ~3% to ~$4,455/oz as dollar strength and rate hike repricing hit the metal hard. The Dow eked flat at 53,559, while the Russell 2000 underperformed with a -0.50% decline, reflecting acute small-cap sensitivity to the higher-for-longer rate narrative.

Heading into Monday's open (Aug 31), the dominant macro theme is the hawkish Fed pivot risk. With PCE still running hot and Warsh signaling discomfort, bond markets face further selling pressure and growth/rate-sensitive sectors remain vulnerable. The week ahead brings ISM Manufacturing (Sep 2) and the August Jobs Report (Sep 5), both critical for determining whether the Fed acts in September. Biotech remains a bright spot with 29 novel FDA approvals in 2026 versus 21 in the same period last year, and the IPO pipeline is building — Aggreko (AGKO) filed for a $1B NYSE listing and Anthropic plans to unveil its prospectus after Labor Day. AI monetization and data center infrastructure stories continue to offer compelling longs on dips.

ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech pushed September rate hike odds to 57% from 35%, with PCE at 3.7% and 54% of the basket above 3%.
ideas.thesis: The bond market had been pricing an easing cycle; Warsh's explicit inflation hawkishness materially shifts that narrative and should push long-duration yields higher into the Sep FOMC meeting. TLT is the cleanest expression of this trade with high liquidity and leverage available via options.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise soft inflation print or significant risk-off event could force a rapid dovish pivot, squeezing TLT shorts.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia delivered a blockbuster earnings outlook that initially sparked a Nasdaq rally before being partially given back on macro headwinds, leaving the stock at an attractive entry.
ideas.thesis: Nvidia's data center revenue continues to accelerate as hyperscalers expand GPU capacity for AI training and inference workloads; the dip on macro fears creates a tactical long entry ahead of continued AI spending cycle. Morgan Stanley has flagged NVDA as a top pick, and the narrative is shifting from capex to applications monetization which broadens the bull case.
ideas.key_risk: A September rate hike that materially tightens financial conditions could compress growth multiples across the AI complex.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs added AON to its August Conviction Buy list with a $276 target, citing 28% upside on stronger-than-consensus 2026 organic growth and accelerating NFP acquisition synergies.
ideas.thesis: AON's integration of NFP is tracking ahead of schedule, driving incremental fee income and margin expansion that the Street has yet to fully model; the insurance brokerage sector is a natural inflation hedge providing earnings resilience even in a higher-rate environment. Goldman's conviction list placement typically attracts significant institutional flow.
ideas.key_risk: Integration delays or unexpected liability from NFP's book could disappoint in subsequent quarters.

ideas.catalyst: Gold slid ~3% to ~$4,455/oz Friday as dollar index surged 0.50% to 99.65 and rate hike odds jumped; the metal is highly sensitive to real yield shifts.
ideas.thesis: Gold peaked as a safe-haven and inflation hedge narrative earlier in 2026; with the Fed now signaling potential rate hikes, real yields are rising and the dollar is strengthening, both direct headwinds for non-yielding bullion. The 3% single-day drop signals a regime shift in gold positioning that could extend over weeks.
ideas.key_risk: Geopolitical escalation or a flight-to-safety event could rapidly reverse the dollar-strength thesis.

ideas.catalyst: FDA decision expected on Gilead's once-daily single-tablet HIV regimen (bictegravir + lenacapavir) combining two of its best-selling agents; Trodelvy also received EU approval, expanding the revenue base.
ideas.thesis: Gilead's HIV franchise generates durable, high-margin recurring revenue and the new once-daily pill — if approved — would consolidate market leadership by simplifying treatment for already-controlled patients, driving switching activity. With 29 novel FDA approvals in 2026 versus 21 in the same period of 2025, regulatory tailwinds support the biotech sector broadly.
ideas.key_risk: A Complete Response Letter or label restrictions on the HIV combination pill would remove a key near-term catalyst.

ideas.catalyst: Piper Sandler downgraded Trupanion from Overweight to Neutral and slashed the price target from $45 to $32, implying ~29% downside from recent levels.
ideas.thesis: Trupanion faces a structural margin squeeze as veterinary cost inflation outpaces premium pricing power, with the higher-rate environment elevating the hurdle rate for growth-stage insurance companies. The Piper downgrade signals deteriorating confidence in the near-term path to profitability and will likely prompt further institutional selling.
ideas.key_risk: A meaningful deceleration in vet cost inflation or unexpected improvement in loss ratios could trigger a short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: Russell 2000 fell 0.50% Friday while S&P 500 declined only 0.25% — small-caps underperforming sharply as rate hike repricing hits floating-rate debt-laden smaller companies disproportionately.
ideas.thesis: Small-cap companies carry significantly higher floating-rate debt burdens than large caps, and a September rate hike would directly increase their interest expense and compress free cash flow; IWM short is a high-beta expression of the hawkish Fed theme with better risk-adjusted returns than single-stock rate plays. The relative underperformance trend that began Friday typically persists for several weeks when rate expectations shift materially.
ideas.key_risk: A soft landing data surprise or Fed pause could spark a violent small-cap catch-up rally.

ideas.catalyst: FDA approved BMS's Zenbexus (iberdomide) in combination with daratumumab and dexamethasone for multiple myeloma on August 19, adding a meaningful label expansion for the company's growing oncology pipeline.
ideas.thesis: BMS's oncology franchise continues to generate regulatory wins — Zenbexus adds to a string of approvals that strengthen recurring prescribing revenue in the high-value multiple myeloma space; with a robust pipeline and a now-diversified revenue base post-Celgene integration, BMS trades at a meaningful discount to biopharma peers on a forward earnings basis. The stock's dividend yield provides downside support in a rising rate environment.
ideas.key_risk: Patent cliff exposure on legacy products and potential pricing pressure from IRA drug negotiation could weigh on longer-term revenue.

ideas.catalyst: Piper Sandler analyst David Westenberg upgraded Neogen from Neutral to Overweight and raised the price target from $13 to $14, citing improving demand trends in food safety testing.
ideas.thesis: Neogen operates in the non-discretionary food safety and animal safety testing market, providing resilient recurring revenue from regulatory compliance demand that is largely insulated from economic cycles; the Piper upgrade signals an inflection point in order flow that could catalyze earnings revisions higher across the next two quarters. At $14 target, the stock offers an attractive risk/reward from current depressed levels.
ideas.key_risk: Integration costs from prior acquisitions could weigh on near-term free cash flow and delay earnings recovery.

ideas.catalyst: National Bank Financial analyst Ahmed Abdullah downgraded Nutrien from Outperform to Sector Perform, citing deteriorating fertilizer pricing dynamics and weakening farmer cash flows.
ideas.thesis: Nutrien's potash and nitrogen earnings are highly leveraged to fertilizer spot prices, which have been under pressure as global supply from key producers normalizes; a stronger dollar — which accelerated Friday on Warsh's hawkishness — further pressures commodity prices broadly and reduces the competitiveness of Canadian exporters like Nutrien. The downgrade removes a key buyer support and signals a longer-than-expected trough in the ag cycle.
ideas.key_risk: A crop failure event (drought, flood) or supply disruption could rapidly reset fertilizer prices upward.

deals.headline: Madison Air Agrees to Acquire Airflow Technologies for $5.4 Billion
deals.description: Madison Air announced an agreement to acquire Airflow Technologies for $5.4 billion in a deal that extends Madison's reach into the HVAC and industrial airflow control markets. The acquisition is expected to close in Q4 2026 pending regulatory approvals and represents one of the largest industrial deals of the summer.
deals.sentiment: Bullish for Airflow (acquisition premium); mixed for Madison (integration risk, leverage)

deals.headline: Aggreko Files for $1 Billion NYSE IPO (Ticker: AGKO) at ~$15B Valuation
deals.description: Glasgow-based temporary-power and energy-infrastructure provider Aggreko filed for a U.S. IPO on the NYSE under ticker AGKO, with an expected offering of approximately $1 billion and a reported valuation of around $15 billion. The company's first-half 2026 revenue surged 28% to ~$1.92 billion driven by accelerating data center demand for temporary power during construction and capacity expansion phases.
deals.sentiment: Bullish — data center tailwind, strong revenue growth, premium valuation

deals.headline: Alibaba to Sell Video Game Division for $1.5B+
deals.description: Alibaba announced plans to sell its video game business unit for at least $1.5 billion as part of an ongoing portfolio rationalization strategy aimed at sharpening focus on core e-commerce and cloud infrastructure businesses. The divestiture is part of a broader restructuring that has seen the company shed non-core assets and return capital to shareholders throughout 2026.
deals.sentiment: Bullish for BABA — capital return potential, strategic clarity; bearish for gaming unit buyer if overpaying

deals.headline: Ursa Major Merges with Bleichroeder SPAC at $2.3B Valuation with $350M PIPE
deals.description: Aerospace and defense technology company Ursa Major agreed to go public through a merger with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. III at a post-transaction equity valuation of approximately $2.3 billion, supported by at least $350 million of PIPE financing led by Inflection Point. Ursa Major develops advanced propulsion systems for hypersonic and space launch vehicles, positioning it at the intersection of defense modernization and commercial space.
deals.sentiment: Bullish — defense sector tailwind, large PIPE anchor, hypersonic demand growing

deals.headline: Deutsche Telekom Acquires Fiberhost and Inea from Macquarie for ~€1 Billion
deals.description: Deutsche Telekom announced it would acquire Polish fiber broadband operators Fiberhost and Inea from Macquarie Asset Management for approximately €1 billion, consolidating its Central European fiber footprint and adding roughly 1.5 million homes passed in Poland. The deal accelerates DT's pan-European fiber strategy and is expected to be marginally accretive to EBITDA within two years.
deals.sentiment: Bullish for DT — European fiber consolidation play, strategic fit; neutral for Macquarie (capital recycling)
